questions.element: /frontier LEAD CHANGES section rule against the block it introduces
questions.note: S5 is ok on every route it samples (entry head/prose, the FACTS heading, /data's four headings, /blog .rail-posts, /catalog's preamble summary, /colophon), but /frontier is unsampled and its LEAD CHANGES rule spans the shell (~1150px, measured off the 1440 capture) over a block near 600px wide — the overhang S5 already closed twice, at I35 and I40.

invariants.txt states it exactly — .entry-side 665.7px reaches only 34.5% of .prose's 1928.0px against a 60% floor, 'a column held open beside nothing for the remaining 1262.3px' — and wiki-entry--light--1440.png confirms the FACTS/RAILS stack ending near a third of the prose run; home is not the failing clause (82.8% of .rail-changes).

Every load-bearing number is read from invariants.txt (34.5%, 665.7px, 1928.0px, 1262.3px, 82.8%) or measured from a file (PNG IHDR dimensions: 928, 937, 390x3041, 768x1693, 768x1408); the one exception is q6's ~1150px rule over a ~600px block, off a downscaled render and stated as approximate — the 2x ratio, not the figure, carries it.

findings.problem: /frontier, the packet's flagship route, has page-level horizontal scroll at both narrow bands: its document is 928px wide at a 390 viewport and 937px at 768, because THE BOARD keeps its 3-column desktop table at every width. Every other captured route matches its viewport exactly (PNG IHDR widths).
findings.invariant: At 390, 768 and 1440, /frontier's document scrollWidth equals the viewport width — equivalently, its full-page capture is exactly viewport-wide, as all ten ported labels' captures are.
findings.prescription: Give the board the reflow /catalog already ships below 33.999rem — one <details> or stacked record per organisation carrying its per-index cells — instead of a table that must be scrolled sideways.

findings.problem: The reflow oracle is green over F-struct-1 because /frontier is not in its sample: verify-design tests 320px on /, /wiki/concept/ai-winter, /catalog and /tools only, while its own coverage line reports 676 exported routes.
findings.invariant: Every route a packet adds appears in the reflow sample and in the route list of each S-check whose property it can violate (S5, S17, S18 at minimum) before that packet is judged.
findings.prescription: Add /frontier to the reflow list and to S5/S17/S18's route lists; a new-route checklist in IMPLEMENT.md generalises it.

findings.problem: On /frontier's claims grid the 'claimed · unverified' chip is bordered on 16 of 16 cells — a value identical across the whole collection drawn as an exception marker, so the box says 'this one differs' where nothing does. The same build applies R8 correctly on /wiki's index.
findings.invariant: On the claims grid a chip renders bordered only where its tone differs from the collection's own dominant state; where one value covers more than 90% of cells it renders unboxed and is stated once above the grid.
findings.prescription: State 'no vendor claim on this site is verified yet' once under the section lede, drop the per-cell border, and keep the box in reserve for the first verified cell.

findings.problem: S18's wiki-entry clause is still failing at 34.5%, and this packet's own reuse line promised to close it ('facts and timeline share the spine track, filling S18's dead column'). The relocation moved ai-winter from ~23% to 34.5% against a 60% floor — under half the distance, on the site's most numerous template (495 pages).
findings.invariant: On a prose wiki entry at 1440 the shorter of .prose / .entry-side reaches 60% of the taller, or the template drops to one column when the content ratio cannot reach it, so no column is held open beside nothing.
findings.prescription: Take the content-ratio single-column fallback R13's iter-09 addendum names and the IR left unattempted: below a measured ratio, render the side stack inline after the lede rather than as a second column.

findings.problem: /frontier's LEAD CHANGES rule spans the page shell over a block roughly half its width — the rule-overhang shape S5 has now closed twice (I35 on /blog, I40 on /catalog), recurring immediately on the one route S5 does not sample.
findings.invariant: On /frontier every section rule's rendered width equals the widest rendered line of the block it introduces, within the tolerance S5 already uses on the routes it samples.
findings.prescription: Give the frontier sections the width: fit-content mechanism .browse and .rail-posts already use, or widen the sparse sections' content to the rule.

carried_forward: IR declined: CatalogFilter wired to the grouped view — the packet's own fence says CatalogFilter unchanged, so the form is CSS-hidden at <=390. Accepted, not re-filed; S8 and S22 hold without it.

IR declined: the site-wide spine on link indexes, per JV-hier F-hier-1 (R8 is a per-surface test, not global chrome). Accepted; /wiki, /tools, /blog and /tutorials read as uniform link indexes at 768.
L7 (seven model pages render 'not published' mid-sentence) is Desk backlog, not filed.

diagnosis.strongest: TABL on /catalog: the flagship table holds its corridor and trailing-column discipline at 1440 (S7, S11, S17, S19 all ok) and its 390 form is a real reduction — a 3,041px document against the 93,963px baseline, groups closed, no sideways scroll.
diagnosis.weakest: RESP on the new route: /frontier is the only surface in the build whose document is wider than its viewport, at both narrow bands, and it is the route the concept exists to deliver.
diagnosis.critical_issue: /frontier has page-level horizontal scroll at 390 (928px document) and 768 (937px), invisible to every gate because the reflow check samples four routes and /frontier is not among them.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Reflow THE BOARD below the shell width with the provider-<details> treatment /catalog already ships, and add /frontier to the reflow sample so the next capture proves it instead of a judge measuring PNG headers.

downstream.weakness: Four of my five findings sit on /frontier, and each is a property an existing S-check or the reflow list already tests elsewhere.
downstream.cause: A packet may add a route without adding it to any check's route list, so the newest surface is the least verified in the build while every gate reports green.
downstream.recommendation: Make route-list extension part of the implementer contract: a new route joins the reflow sample and every S-check whose property it can violate before the evidence run, and the IR states which lists it joined.
